key_insight: A recurrent neural network trained for free recall can independently discover multiple memory strategies, including human-like ones that go beyond classical temporal-context explanations. The strongest models appear to use an index-based recall mechanism similar to the memory palace technique.
problem_solved: This paper addresses how free recall can be modeled more realistically than with traditional temporal context models, which often assume memory retrieval is driven mainly by recent sequence context. It asks whether neural networks can learn richer, diverse strategies that better match human memory behavior.
method: Train recurrent neural networks on free-recall tasks and optimize them to reproduce recall behavior.
Compare the learned mechanisms against classical temporal context models and identify distinct strategy types.
Analyze top-performing models to infer how they store and retrieve items, revealing index-based recall behavior.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows that end-to-end training can uncover interpretable memory strategies rather than only fitting behavior with hand-designed assumptions. It may inspire better sequence models, memory-augmented systems, and more human-like retrieval mechanisms.

paper_title: A neural network model of free recall learns multiple memory strategies
paper_authors: Moufan Li, Kristopher T. Jensen, Qiong Zhang, Qihong Lu, Marcelo G. Mattar
